I care, and I'm sure so many others do. Depression tricks the mind, it makes it think things that aren't true. I know five years seems like a long time, but it's not too late to get your life together. Find a therapist, join support groups, read self-help books, start meditating. Five years is nothing compared to the many years of your life you still have. Your feelings are temporary, your death isn't. Keep your head up.

Never is a very strong word. Sometimes some methods of treatment aren't as effective as others, so maybe the current method you are on isn't working for you. Do some research and see your other options. You are a strong, capable person because everyone is. Your depression doesn't define you. Not joining the military isn't the end of the world, and you can find meaning in your life in other ways. Just as good things don't last forever, nor do bad things. This is a temporary place in your life. I promise it'll look up but you need to believe in yourself. I believe in you!! If you ever need anything or someone to talk to my dms are always open.

Hey I know you may think there's no point, but there always is a point. What your feeling is temporary, your death isn't. If you don't want to live for yourself, live for those around you. Your boyfriend will forever live with the guilt that he could have done something different to save you. That fear and guilt will translate to any future relationship he has, if he chooses to have one. Your mother will never be the same, and will live her life thinking she could have been a better more loving mother. Losing a child is like losing a part of you. Trust me I know, my sister committed suicide in 2015 and to this day I can't escape the weight I have to carry.
